# `silk/encoding/pem`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Read and write PEM, the Base64 text armor for keys and certificates (RFC 7468).

## When to use
Use [`Pem`](#Pem) to find the `-----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY-----` style blocks in text and get their DER
bytes, or to wrap DER bytes in such a block, for example for `createPrivateKey` and `export` in
Node.js. The DER itself is read by the key modules, such as `silk.crypto.rsa`.

## Details
[`Pem.find`](#Pem.impl.find) returns the next block at or after an offset as a [`PemSection`](#PemSection) of offsets into the
input, so nothing is copied. Text before, between, and after blocks is skipped. Inside a block
the Base64 may wrap at any width and may hold spaces, tabs, and CR or LF line ends, as OpenSSL
allows. RFC 1421 headers such as `Proc-Type` and `DEK-Info`, which a legacy encrypted key has,
end at the first empty line and can be read with [`Pem.header`](#Pem.impl.header). [`Pem.encode`](#Pem.impl.encode) writes such
headers when given, then Base64 lines of 64 characters, with LF line ends. Nothing allocates.

## Errors
The functions return a [`PemError`](#PemError). On an error the output does not change.

## Gotchas
The Base64 of a block must be canonical: padding only at the end, and zero unused bits. A label
is not checked against a list; compare [`Pem.label`](#Pem.impl.label) with the one you expect.

## Examples
### Round trip a block
```silk
import silk.encoding.pem { Pem, PemError, PemSection }
import silk.core.result { Result }

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  let mut text: [u8; 64] = [0; 64]
  let length = match Pem.encode(b"TEST", b"", b"hello", &mut text) {
    Result<usize, PemError>.Success { value } => value
    Result<usize, PemError>.Failure { error: _ } => {
      return 1
    }
  }
  if length != Pem.encodedLength(4, 0, 5) {
    return 1
  }
  let section = match Pem.find(&text, 0) {
    Result<PemSection, PemError>.Success { value } => move value
    Result<PemSection, PemError>.Failure { error: _ } => {
      return 1
    }
  }
  let label = Pem.label(&text, &section)
  if label.length != 4 || label[0] != 84 {
    return 1
  }
  let mut bytes: [u8; 8] = [0; 8]
  let decoded = match Pem.decode(&text, &section, &mut bytes) {
    Result<usize, PemError>.Success { value } => value
    Result<usize, PemError>.Failure { error: _ } => {
      return 1
    }
  }
  if decoded != 5 || bytes[0] != 104 || bytes[4] != 111 {
    return 1
  }
  return 0
}
```

<a id="PemSection"></a>

## `PemSection`

```silk
pub struct PemSection
```

One PEM block, as offsets into the text that [`Pem.find`](#Pem.impl.find) read.

### Details

The label is `labelStart` to `labelEnd`, the RFC 1421 headers are `headersStart` to `headersEnd`
(empty when there are none), and the Base64 body is `bodyStart` to `bodyEnd`. The block ends at
`end`, after the END line, where the next search can start.

<a id="PemSection.start"></a>

```silk
pub start: usize
```

The offset of the `-----BEGIN` line.

<a id="Pem.impl.find"></a>

### Associated function `find`

```silk
pub fn find(input: &[u8], offset: usize) -> Result<PemSection, PemError>
```

Returns the next PEM block that starts at or after `offset` of `input`.

#### Errors

- `NotFound` if no `-----BEGIN ` line starts at or after `offset`.
- `Malformed` if the first such block is broken, or its END line is missing or has another
  label.

<a id="Pem.impl.label"></a>

### Associated function `label`

```silk
pub fn label<'a>(input: &'a [u8], section: &PemSection) -> &'a [u8]
```

Returns the label of `section`, such as `PRIVATE KEY`.

<a id="Pem.impl.header"></a>

### Associated function `header`

```silk
pub fn header<'a>(input: &'a [u8], section: &PemSection, name: &[u8]) -> Option<&'a [u8]>
```

Returns the value of the RFC 1421 header `name` of `section`, such as `DEK-Info`, without the
spaces around it, or `None` if the block has no such header.

The name compares exactly. A header that continues on the next line is not joined.

<a id="Pem.impl.decode"></a>

### Associated function `decode`

```silk
pub fn decode(input: &[u8], section: &PemSection, output: &mut [u8]) -> Result<usize, PemError>
```

Decodes the Base64 body of `section` into `output` and returns the number of bytes written.

#### Errors

- `Malformed` if the body is not canonical Base64 once spaces, tabs, CR, and LF are removed.
- `OutputTooSmall` if `output` is shorter than the decoded bytes.

<a id="Pem.impl.encodedLength"></a>

### Associated function `encodedLength`

```silk
pub fn encodedLength(labelLength: usize, headersLength: usize, length: usize) -> usize
```

Returns the number of bytes that [`Pem.encode`](#Pem.impl.encode) writes for a label of `labelLength` bytes,
`headersLength` bytes of headers, and `length` bytes of data.

<a id="Pem.impl.encode"></a>

### Associated function `encode`

```silk
pub fn encode(label: &[u8], headers: &[u8], bytes: &[u8], output: &mut [u8]) -> Result<usize, PemError>
```

Writes `bytes` as a PEM block with label `label` to `output` and returns the number of bytes
written, [`Pem.encodedLength`](#Pem.impl.encodedLength).

`headers` is empty, or RFC 1421 header lines that each end with LF, such as
`Proc-Type: 4,ENCRYPTED\nDEK-Info: AES-256-CBC,...\n`; the empty line after them is added.
The Base64 lines have 64 characters and LF line ends.

#### Errors

- `InvalidLabel` if `label` is empty, or holds a byte outside printable ASCII or a `-`.
- `Malformed` if `headers` is not empty and does not end with LF, or holds an empty line.
- `OutputTooSmall` if `output` is shorter than [`Pem.encodedLength`](#Pem.impl.encodedLength).
